name: Acesulfame K
aliases: E950, acesulfame K, acesulfame potassium, Ace-K, acesulfame K sweetener, potassium salt of acesulfame
what_is: A high-intensity non-nutritive sweetener used to provide sweetness in foods and beverages, often in combination with other sweeteners.
why_botia: BOTIA flags it because E950 is a high-intensity sweetener whose permitted uses and maximum levels vary between regulatory systems and can be used in synergistic blends with other sweeteners.
can_1: Identify E950 or acesulfame K when declared on the label.
can_2: Trigger the E-number and sweetener information layers.
cannot_1: Determine the quantity used from the ingredient list alone or whether it forms part of a sweetener blend.
cannot_2: Determine total dietary exposure or make a medical or nutritional judgement for an individual user.

sources.label: FDA — Aspartame and Other Sweeteners in Food
